---
title: "Quiz: learning"
---

Short questions on losses, gradient descent, backpropagation and overfitting. Try each on paper first, then open the answer. Cross-entropy is $-\ln p_\text{true class}$; a gradient step is $\mathbf w \leftarrow \mathbf w - \eta\nabla\mathcal L$.

---

**Q1.** A network gives the true class probability 0.8 for one image and 0.05 for another. What is the cross-entropy of each?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$-\ln p$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$-\ln 0.8 = 0.22$ and $-\ln 0.05 = 3.00$. The confident mistake costs about 13 times as much.
:::

---

**Q2.** You train with full-batch gradient descent and the loss grows from step to step. What do you change first?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What sets the length of each step?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Lower the learning rate $\eta$: each step overshoots the valley and lands higher than it started.
:::

---

**Q3.** 50,000 training images, mini-batches of 100. How many gradient steps is one epoch? What changes if you use batches of 10?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
An epoch is one pass over all images.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
500 steps. With batches of 10: 5,000 steps per epoch, each cheaper but noisier (the gradient estimate from 10 images varies more).
:::

---

**Q4.** In the backward pass, a ReLU unit had $z = -2$ in the forward pass. What gradient does it pass back to its weights?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The local derivative of $\max(0, z)$ at $z < 0$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Zero: the ReLU's local derivative is 0 for $z < 0$, so every gradient behind it is multiplied by 0. For this example the unit's weights do not change. If that holds for every training example, the unit is dead.
:::

---

**Q5.** Why is backpropagation so much cheaper than estimating each $\partial\mathcal L/\partial w$ by changing $w$ a little and recomputing the loss?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Count forward passes for a network with a million weights.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Finite differences need one extra forward pass per weight: a million forward passes. Backpropagation gets all million gradients from one forward and one backward pass, at about twice the cost of a forward pass, because it reuses the gradient of each node for everything behind it.
:::

---

**Q6.** The training loss keeps falling, the validation loss has been rising for 50 epochs. What is happening, and which weights do you keep?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Learning curves.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The network is overfitting: it memorises the training examples, and gets worse on new ones. Keep the weights from the epoch with the lowest validation loss (early stopping), or regularise and train again.
:::

---

**Q7.** Name three ways to reduce overfitting.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Penalty, noise, data.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Weight decay (a penalty on large weights), dropout (silence random units during training), more data or data augmentation. Also: a smaller network, early stopping.
:::

---

**Q8.** *(math)* For softmax followed by cross-entropy, what is $\partial\mathcal L/\partial z_k$? Evaluate it for $\mathbf p = (0.7, 0.2, 0.1)$ when the true class is the second.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Predicted minus wanted.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$\partial\mathcal L/\partial z_k = p_k - y_k$: $(0.7, 0.2 - 1, 0.1) = (0.7, -0.8, 0.1)$. A step against it lowers $z_1$ and $z_3$ and raises $z_2$.
:::
